newsitem.title: USA: NC police probe death of bus hijacker.
newsitem.headline: NC police probe death of bus hijacker.

text.p: Police said Friday they were nearly finished with their investigation to determine whether charges should be filed against passengers who overpowered a man who died during a Greyhound bus hijacking.
"The case will be taken to the district attorney and a final decision will be made with them," Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department investigator R.K. Harris said.
Christopher Duffner, 26, of Covington, Kentucky, died after being overpowered by the driver and passengers aboard a Greyhound bus commandeered north of Columbia, South Carolina, on July 19.
Passengers said Duffner took control of the bus by holding a sharp metal object to the driver's throat, Harris said. There were about 30 people on board.
The passengers made a "collective decision" to retake control when Duffner drove the bus erratically along Interstate 77 to Charlotte.
"The passengers felt that their lives were in danger," he said.
Some passengers scuffled with Duffner and the bus collided with a concrete barrier "in the process of them attempting to subdue and detain the individual," Harris said.
Duffner was unconscious when police arrived and died a short time later, he said.
North Carolina law allows crime victims to use whatever force is necessary to subdue a criminal if there is an imminent threat of serious injury or death.
Harris said he expected to meet with prosecutors next week to determine whether charges should be filed in Duffner's death.
